The note is incorrect: a catheter valve does not track or measure urine volume, so recorded urine volumes are not a reason to use one. Do not use a valve when the patient cannot sense bladder fullness or operate it (cognitive impairment, poor dexterity), has inadequate bladder capacity or high-risk retention, or has UTI, hematuria, or obstruction needing continuous drainage, including acute illness, post-urologic surgery, or when accurate fluid balance monitoring is required.
CONFIDENCE: 88
